rationale:
The supplied proof (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2, "only if"; parent steps 1–7) splits into four reusable mathematical obligations:
(1) immersion_injective — the analytic half of step 5. A C¹ map whose derivative is injective at x is injective, with injective derivatives, on a closed ball around x. This uses an anti-Lipschitz lower bound, continuity of DG and the mean value inequality.
(2) ball_chart — the topological half of step 5. If a C¹ map is injective on B̄_r(x) and has injective derivative on B_r(x), then G(B_r(x)) is an embedded C¹ m-submanifold. Take V = B_r(x), ψ = G and W = ℝ^P ∖ G(∂B_r(x)); the parent's annulus is reduced to the sphere, the only part its properness argument uses.
(3) c1_range_cover — steps 4 and 6. The range of one C¹ map is an H^m-null set (SimonGMT area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero) plus countably many embedded C¹ m-submanifolds (Lindelöf); it uses (1) and (2).
(4) lipschitz_c1_pieces — steps 2–3. A Lipschitz map agrees with countably many C¹ maps off a set whose image is H^m-null. The scalar C¹ approximation enters as the hypothesis (H).

Why (H) is a hypothesis: new children may only depend on their own siblings. So (4) takes as (H) the exact frozen type of the selected node's resolved dependency c1_approx (dor_lmbsf_lipschitz_c1_approx) at dimension m. subproblems.title: A C¹ map is injective, with injective derivatives, on a closed ball around a point where its derivative is injective
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (G : Euclid m → Euclid P) (x : Euclid m), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ G x) → ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ Set.InjOn G (Metric.closedBall x r) ∧ ∀ z ∈ Metric.closedBall x r, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ G z)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 1.2, 'only if' part (chapter-03.txt lines 61–65): 'if the Jacobian of G_ij is non-zero at a point x, then there is a σ > 0 such that G_ij(B_σ(x)) is an n-dimensional C¹ submanifold'. This child is the analytic first half of step 5 of the parent proof: the choice of c and ρ, the mean value inequality and injectivity. Notation: L := DG(x); ‖A‖ denotes the operator norm of a linear map A.

1. Lower bound for L. L is an injective linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^m, so ker L = 0 and L is anti-Lipschitz: there is K > 0 with |v| ≤ K|Lv| for all v ∈ ℝ^m. (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith, applied to L as a linear map with ker = ⊥ from LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, gives AntilipschitzWith K L. Applying it to v and 0 gives |v| ≤ K|Lv|.) For m ≥ 1, 1/K plays the role of c = min_{|v|=1}|Lv| > 0 in the parent proof. For m = 0 every vector is 0 and the bound is trivial. Put c := 1/K > 0. Then c|v| ≤ |Lv| for every v ∈ ℝ^m.

2. Choice of r. Since G is C¹, z ↦ DG(z) is continuous into the space of linear maps with the operator norm (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, using 1 ≠ 0). So there is δ > 0 with ‖DG(z) − L‖ < c/2 whenever |z − x| < δ. Put r := δ/2 > 0. Every z ∈ B̄_r(x) has |z − x| ≤ δ/2 < δ. Hence ‖DG(z) − L‖ ≤ c/2 for every z ∈ B̄_r(x).

3. Injective derivatives on B̄_r(x). Let z ∈ B̄_r(x) and v, w ∈ ℝ^m with DG(z)v = DG(z)w. Put u := v − w. By linearity DG(z)u = 0, so Lu = Lu − DG(z)u = −(DG(z) − L)u. By steps 1 and 2,
   c|u| ≤ |Lu| = |(DG(z) − L)u| ≤ ‖DG(z) − L‖·|u| ≤ (c/2)|u|.
   Since c > 0, this gives |u| ≤ 0, so u = 0 and v = w. Hence DG(z) is injective.

4. Mean value inequality. The closed ball B̄_r(x) is convex, G is differentiable at each of its points (G is C¹), and ‖DG(z) − L‖ ≤ c/2 for z ∈ B̄_r(x) by step 2. Apply the mean value inequality to G − L on B̄_r(x) (Mathlib Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le' with φ = L and C = c/2). For all a, b ∈ B̄_r(x):
   |G(a) − G(b) − L(a − b)| ≤ (c/2)|a − b|.

5. G is injective on B̄_r(x). Let a, b ∈ B̄_r(x) with G(a) = G(b). Then G(a) − G(b) = 0 and |−L(a − b)| = |L(a − b)|, so step 4 reads |L(a − b)| ≤ (c/2)|a − b|. Step 1 gives c|a − b| ≤ |L(a − b)|. Hence c|a − b| ≤ (c/2)|a − b|. As c > 0, |a − b| = 0 and a = b.

6. Conclusion. r = δ/2 > 0, G is injective on B̄_r(x) by step 5, and DG(z) is injective for every z ∈ B̄_r(x) by step 3. ∎

Lean notes (checked in a scratch file):
- Steps 1–2: `(fderiv ℝ G x : Euclid m →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P).exists_antilipschitzWith (LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.2 hx)`, then `hK.le_mul_dist v 0`, `inv_mul_le_iff₀`, `hG.continuous_fderiv (by norm_num)` and `Metric.continuous_iff`.
- Step 4: `(convex_closedBall x r).norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le'`.
- Steps 3 and 5: `ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm`; conclude with nlinarith from c‖u‖ ≤ (c/2)‖u‖.
proof_key_steps: DG(x) is injective on the finite-dimensional ℝ^m, hence anti-Lipschitz: c|v| ≤ |DG(x)v| for some c > 0.
Continuity of DG gives r > 0 with ‖DG(z) − DG(x)‖ ≤ c/2 on B̄_r(x).
Then c|u| ≤ |DG(x)u| = |(DG(z) − DG(x))u| ≤ (c/2)|u| whenever DG(z)u = 0, so DG(z) is injective on B̄_r(x).
Mean value inequality on the convex ball: |G(a) − G(b) − DG(x)(a − b)| ≤ (c/2)|a − b|.
If G(a) = G(b), then c|a − b| ≤ (c/2)|a − b|, so a = b: G is injective on B̄_r(x).

subproblems.title: The image of an open ball under a C¹ immersion that is injective on the closed ball is an embedded C¹ submanifold
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (G : Euclid m → Euclid P) (x : Euclid m) (r : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → Set.InjOn G (Metric.closedBall x r) → (∀ z ∈ Metric.ball x r, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ G z)) → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m (G '' Metric.ball x r)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 1.2, chapter-03.txt lines 61–64: 'G_ij(B_σ(x)) is an n-dimensional C¹ submanifold … (with G_ij providing a local representation in a neighborhood of the point y = G_ij(x))'. The printed 'submanifold of ℝ^n' is a misprint for ℝ^{n+ℓ}. This child is the chart half of step 5 of the parent proof, with V = B_ρ(x) and ψ = G. The parent takes W = ℝ^P ∖ G(B̄_{2ρ}(x) ∖ B_ρ(x)). Its properness argument uses only the sphere ∂B_ρ(x) inside that annulus. So here W := ℝ^P ∖ G(∂B_r(x)), and injectivity is needed only on B̄_r(x).

Notation:
- S := {z ∈ ℝ^m : |z − x| = r}, the sphere; S ⊆ B̄_r(x) and S ∩ B_r(x) = ∅.
- V := B_r(x), W := ℝ^P ∖ G(S), ψ := G, N := G(V).

1. W and V are open. S is closed and bounded in ℝ^m, hence compact (Mathlib isCompact_sphere). G is continuous because it is C¹, so G(S) is compact and hence closed in the Hausdorff space ℝ^P. So W is open. V is an open ball, so V is open.

2. N ⊆ W. Let y ∈ N, say y = G(v) with v ∈ V. Suppose y ∈ G(S), say y = G(s) with s ∈ S. Both v ∈ B_r(x) ⊆ B̄_r(x) and s ∈ S ⊆ B̄_r(x), and G is injective on B̄_r(x), so s = v. But |v − x| < r = |s − x|, a contradiction. Hence y ∉ G(S), that is, y ∈ W.

3. Fix y ∈ N. We check the defining conditions of IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m N at y with the data (V, W, ψ), which are the same for every y.
   (a) V and W are open by step 1, and y ∈ W by step 2.
   (b) ψ = G is C¹ on V: G is C¹ on ℝ^m, so ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G V (ContDiff.contDiffOn; the contract's order is the natural number 1 cast to WithTop ℕ∞).
   (c) ψ is injective on V, because V ⊆ B̄_r(x) and G is injective on B̄_r(x).
   (d) ψ(V) = W ∩ N. Indeed ψ(V) = N by definition, and N ⊆ W by step 2, so W ∩ N = N = ψ(V).
   (e) Properness. Let K ⊆ W be compact. We claim V ∩ G⁻¹(K) = B̄_r(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K).
       - The inclusion ⊆ holds because V ⊆ B̄_r(x).
       - Conversely, let z ∈ B̄_r(x) with G(z) ∈ K. If |z − x| = r, then z ∈ S, so G(z) ∈ G(S) and G(z) ∉ W. This contradicts G(z) ∈ K ⊆ W. Hence |z − x| < r, that is, z ∈ V.
       Now B̄_r(x) is compact (closed balls of ℝ^m are compact; isCompact_closedBall). K is compact, hence closed in ℝ^P, and G is continuous, so G⁻¹(K) is closed. A compact set intersected with a closed set is compact (IsCompact.inter_right). Therefore V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) = B̄_r(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K) is compact.
   (f) For z ∈ V, Dψ(z) = DG(z) is injective by hypothesis.

4. Conclusion. Conditions (a)–(f) hold at every y ∈ N, so IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m N holds. When r ≤ 0, V = ∅ and N = ∅, so there is nothing to check; the argument above does not use r > 0 anyway. ∎

Lean notes (checked in a scratch file):
- Step 1: `((isCompact_sphere x r).image hG.continuous).isClosed.isOpen_compl`.
- Step 3(b): `exact_mod_cast hG.contDiffOn`.
- Step 3(e): `Metric.mem_closedBall`, `lt_or_eq`, `Metric.mem_sphere`, `(isCompact_closedBall x r).inter_right (hK.isClosed.preimage hG.continuous)`.
proof_key_steps: W := ℝ^P ∖ G(∂B_r(x)) is open, because the sphere is compact and G is continuous.
Injectivity of G on B̄_r(x) gives G(B_r(x)) ⊆ W. So with V = B_r(x) and ψ = G, ψ(V) = W ∩ N.
C¹ regularity on V, injectivity on V and injective derivatives follow from the hypotheses.
Properness: for compact K ⊆ W, B_r(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K) = B̄_r(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K), because sphere points map outside W. This is a closed subset of a compact ball, hence compact.

subproblems.title: A Lipschitz map ℝ^m → ℝ^P agrees with countably many C¹ maps off a set with H^m-null image (given scalar C¹ approximation)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0, and let F : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be K-Lipschitz (ℝ^k = Euclid k). Assume:
(H) for every Lipschitz u : ℝ^m → ℝ (with any constant L ≥ 0) and every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is g : ℝ^m → ℝ of class C¹ with L^m({y : u(y) ≠ g(y)}) < ε, where L^m = volume on ℝ^m.
(H) is verbatim the frozen type of the C¹-approximation node c1_approx (Lean dor_lmbsf_lipschitz_c1_approx; Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5, value part) at dimension m.
Then there are E ⊆ ℝ^P with H^m(E) = 0 (H^m = μHE[m]) and C¹ maps G_i : ℝ^m → ℝ^P (i ∈ ℕ) such that F(ℝ^m) ⊆ E ∪ ⋃_i G_i(ℝ^m).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (F : Euclid m → Euclid P) (K : NNReal), LipschitzWith K F → (∀ (u : Euclid m → ℝ) (L : NNReal), LipschitzWith L u → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Euclid m → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ volume {y | u y ≠ g y} < ε) → ∃ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (G : ℕ → Euclid m → Euclid P), μHE[m] E = 0 ∧ (∀ i, ContDiff ℝ 1 (G i)) ∧ Set.range F ⊆ E ∪ ⋃ i, Set.range (G i)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 1.2, 'only if' part, chapter-03.txt lines 39–59. This is steps 2–3 of the parent proof for one Lipschitz map F = F_j.

Printed errata, applied here:
- Lines 41–42: 'G_ij : ℝ^n → ℝ^ℓ' should read ℝ^{n+ℓ}.
- Line 49: 'graph F_j ⊆ E_j ∪ ⋃_i G_ij(ℝ^n)' should read F_j(ℝ^n) ⊆ ….
- Ch. 2 Theorem 1.5 is scalar, so it is applied coordinatewise.

The constants differ harmlessly from the parent's step 2: each coordinate uses ε = 1/i instead of 1/(iP). The resulting bound P/i → 0 replaces 1/i and removes the separate case P = 0.

1. Coordinates are Lipschitz. For p ∈ Fin P let F^p(y) := (F(y))_p. For a ∈ ℝ^P we have |a_p| ≤ |a| (Mathlib PiLp.norm_apply_le). Hence
   |F^p(a) − F^p(b)| = |(F(a) − F(b))_p| ≤ |F(a) − F(b)| ≤ K|a − b|,
   so F^p is K-Lipschitz.

2. Coordinatewise C¹ approximation. Fix i ∈ ℕ and put ε_i := 1/i ∈ (0, ∞]. In [0, ∞] we have 1/0 = ∞, and ε_i > 0 because i < ∞. For each p, apply (H) to u = F^p, L = K and ε = ε_i. This gives a C¹ function g_{ip} : ℝ^m → ℝ with L^m({F^p ≠ g_{ip}}) < 1/i. Define G_i : ℝ^m → ℝ^P by (G_i(y))_p := g_{ip}(y). Each coordinate of G_i is C¹, so G_i is C¹ (Mathlib contDiff_piLp).

3. Disagreement sets are small. If F(y) ≠ G_i(y), then F^p(y) ≠ g_{ip}(y) for some p, since two vectors of ℝ^P with equal coordinates are equal. So {F ≠ G_i} ⊆ ⋃_p {F^p ≠ g_{ip}}. By monotonicity and finite subadditivity of the outer measure L^m (no measurability needed; measure_iUnion_fintype_le):
   L^m({F ≠ G_i}) ≤ Σ_p L^m({F^p ≠ g_{ip}}) ≤ P · (1/i).

4. The bad set is null. Let Z := ⋂_{i∈ℕ} {F ≠ G_i}. For each i, Z ⊆ {F ≠ G_i}, so L^m(Z) ≤ P · (1/i). In [0, ∞], 1/i → 0 as i → ∞, and P < ∞, so P · (1/i) → 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero, ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul). Hence L^m(Z) ≤ 0, that is, L^m(Z) = 0.

5. The image of the bad set is null. Put E := F(Z). F is K-Lipschitz on Z, so H^m(F(Z)) ≤ K^m H^m(Z) (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn with n = m, applied to LipschitzOnWith K F Z). On ℝ^m = Euclid m, H^m = L^m (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume m). So H^m(E) ≤ K^m · L^m(Z) = 0.

6. Covering. Let y ∈ F(ℝ^m), say y = F(z).
   - If z ∈ Z, then y ∈ F(Z) = E.
   - Otherwise z ∉ {F ≠ G_i} for some i, that is, F(z) = G_i(z), so y = G_i(z) ∈ G_i(ℝ^m).
   Hence F(ℝ^m) ⊆ E ∪ ⋃_i G_i(ℝ^m).

7. Conclusion. E and the maps (G_i) have the required properties by steps 2, 5 and 6. ∎

- Coordinates are `(F y).ofLp p`; use `PiLp.sub_apply` and `PiLp.norm_apply_le`.
- `ε := ((i : ℝ≥0∞))⁻¹`, positive by `ENNReal.inv_pos.2 (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top i)`.
- `G i y := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun p => g i p y)` with `(contDiff_piLp 2).2`.
- Step 3: `measure_iUnion_fintype_le`; the sum of constants simplifies to `(P : ℝ≥0∞) * (i)⁻¹`.
- Step 4: `ge_of_tendsto'` with `ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero (Or.inr (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top P))`.
- Step 5: `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn m (hF.lipschitzOnWith (s := Z))`, then rewrite with `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`.
proof_key_steps: The coordinates F^p of F are K-Lipschitz.
Apply (H) to each coordinate with ε = 1/i and assemble the C¹ maps G_i coordinatewise.
Subadditivity over the P coordinates gives L^m({F ≠ G_i}) ≤ P/i.
Z = ⋂_i {F ≠ G_i} is L^m-null, and E = F(Z) is H^m-null by the Lipschitz image bound and H^m = L^m on ℝ^m.
Points off Z satisfy F = G_i for some i, so F(ℝ^m) ⊆ E ∪ ⋃_i G_i(ℝ^m).

subproblems.title: The image of a C¹ map ℝ^m → ℝ^P is covered by an H^m-null set and countably many embedded C¹ m-submanifolds
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (G : Euclid m → Euclid P), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → ∃ (N₀ : Set (Euclid P)) (N : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)), μHE[m] N₀ = 0 ∧ (∀ l, IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m (N l)) ∧ Set.range G ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ l, N l
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 1.2, 'only if' part, last paragraph (chapter-03.txt lines 61–65). This is steps 4 and 6 of the parent proof for a single C¹ map.

Printed errata, applied here:
- Line 61, 'by the area formula L^n({x : JG_ij = 0}', is garbled; it means H^n(G_ij({x : JG_ij = 0})) = 0.
- Line 63, 'submanifold of ℝ^n', should read ℝ^{n+ℓ}.
- Simon leaves the countable selection of balls (Lindelöf) implicit.

Uses siblings:
- immersion_injective (Lean dor_lmbsf_c1c_immersion_local_injOn);
- ball_chart (Lean dor_lmbsf_c1c_injOn_closedBall_chart).
Required import: Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaCritical. It is not in the contract's import closure, so add it to Submission.lean.

1. G is differentiable everywhere. G is C¹, so it is differentiable at every x ∈ ℝ^m (ContDiff.differentiable, 1 ≠ 0).

2. The critical image is null. Let Crit := {x ∈ ℝ^m : G is differentiable at x and DG(x) is not injective}. By step 1, Crit = {x : DG(x) not injective}.
   - Mathematically: by the area formula of Simon Ch. 2 §3, H^m(G(A)) ≤ ∫_A J_G dL^m with J_G = 0 exactly where DG is not injective, so H^m(G(Crit)) = 0.
   - In SimonGMT this is Chapter02.area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero G, with E = ℝ^m = Euclid m and F = ℝ^P. It states μHE[finrank ℝ E](G '' {x | DifferentiableAt ℝ G x ∧ ¬ Injective (fderiv ℝ G x)}) = 0, and finrank ℝ (Euclid m) = m (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
   Put N₀ := G(Crit). Then μHE[m] N₀ = 0.

3. Local charts at regular points. Let R := {x ∈ ℝ^m : DG(x) is injective}. Fix x ∈ R.
   - Sibling immersion_injective, applied to G and x, gives r_x > 0 such that G is injective on B̄_{r_x}(x) and DG(z) is injective for all z ∈ B̄_{r_x}(x).
   - Apply sibling ball_chart to G, x and r = r_x. Its hypotheses hold: G is C¹; G is injective on B̄_{r_x}(x); and DG(z) is injective for z ∈ B_{r_x}(x), since B_{r_x}(x) ⊆ B̄_{r_x}(x).
   Hence G(B_{r_x}(x)) satisfies IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m.

4. Countable subcover (Lindelöf).
   - If R = ∅, put N_l := ∅ for every l. The empty set satisfies IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m vacuously, because the definition quantifies over the points of the set.
   - If R ≠ ∅, the open balls B_{r_x}(x), x ∈ R, cover R, since x ∈ B_{r_x}(x) as r_x > 0. ℝ^m is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf, so R is Lindelöf. So there is a sequence (x_l)_{l∈ℕ} in R with R ⊆ ⋃_l B_{r_{x_l}}(x_l) (Mathlib HereditarilyLindelofSpace.isLindelof R and IsLindelof.indexed_countable_subcover, with the nonempty index type R). Put N_l := G(B_{r_{x_l}}(x_l)). By step 3, each N_l satisfies IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m.

5. Covering. Let y ∈ G(ℝ^m), say y = G(x).
   - If DG(x) is injective, then x ∈ R (so R ≠ ∅). By step 4, x ∈ B_{r_{x_l}}(x_l) for some l, so y ∈ N_l.
   - Otherwise G is differentiable at x (step 1) and DG(x) is not injective, so x ∈ Crit and y ∈ N₀.
   Hence G(ℝ^m) ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_l N_l.

6. Conclusion. N₀ and the sets N_l have all the required properties by steps 2, 4 and 5. ∎
